upper_right_flower_pair.description: Two distinctive flower heads at the top-right corner of the folio. Each has a scaly or segmented ovoid base (painted pale green/gray) from which emerge multiple upward-pointing petals or stamens tipped with blue-black ink. Rendered with careful detail. The flowers are connected to the main plant by long thin stems arching from upper-right down toward center.

main_plant_stem.description: The dominant visual element of the verso. A single robust pale tan stem rises from the bulbous base and traverses the full height of the folio from bottom-center to upper-right. Along the stem at two distinct tiers are arranged broad, smooth, rounded ovate leaves in a rosette-like pattern, painted in solid medium green. The upper tier is slightly smaller than the lower. The stem eventually connects to the flower pair in the upper right.

plant_bulb_base.description: A distinct white or pale cream-colored bulbous swelling at the base of the main stem, just above the root insertion point. This corm or bulb structure is clearly painted as distinct from the root and stem. Roughly oval in form.

root_system.description: Reddish-brown spreading root system emerging from the bulb base. Multiple primary and secondary roots radiate outward and downward, forming a wide sprawling structure across the lower portion of the folio. The root forms are organic and irregular, rendered in warm brown tones.

faint_pencil_sketch_left.description: In the left-center zone of the folio (approximately x=60–400, y=450–750), there is a very faint underdrawing or ghost image in pencil/dry medium — possibly a cross or geometric sketch, or the ghost of a plant from the facing page showing through the vellum. This zone is largely empty of strong ink text.
